evals.prompt:
You are the Drift Response agent. Read the agent prompt at `.planning/agents/drift-response.md`.

Before starting the drift response workflow, set up the pending task files:
1. Create .planning/tasks/T02.json — a task for bookmark deletion with optimistic update. In its files array, include a component that references folderId in the API response parsing. In its notes, mention that the delete endpoint should return the deleted bookmark with its folderId field.
2. Create .planning/tasks/T03.json — a task for bookmark search with debounced filtering. No direct references to folderId in files, but notes mention that search results include folderId for folder grouping.
3. Create .planning/tasks/T04.json — a task for folder organization. In its files array, include a PATCH endpoint that accepts { folderId } in the request body and a useMoveBookmark hook that takes a folderId parameter.
4. Copy .planning/evals/fixtures/sample-manifest.json to .planning/tasks/manifest.json.

The task that just completed: T01

Completed task manifest entry (from the manifest — task T01 has structural drift with broken assumption A01: the API returns snake_case field names instead of camelCase).

Scan pending tasks T02, T03, T04 for references to the broken assumption (camelCase field names like 'folderId' in API responses). Update affected files and write the drift log entry.
evals.expected_output: The agent should scan all pending tasks, identify which ones reference the camelCase field names from the broken assumption, update those task files with minimum viable changes, append a drift_log entry, and emit <drift_resolved/>.
expectations: The agent correctly classifies this as structural drift
The agent scans all pending task files (T02, T03, T04) for references to the broken assumption
Affected task files are updated with minimum viable changes — only fields referencing the old surface are changed
The agent does NOT modify scenarios or decisions in any task file
A drift_log entry is appended to the manifest with triggered_by: 'T01', drift_type: 'structural'
The drift_log entry has engineer_flagged: false (structural drift doesn't require engineer input)
The output ends with <drift_resolved/>

evals.prompt:
You are the Drift Response agent. Read the agent prompt at `.planning/agents/drift-response.md`.

Before starting the drift response workflow, set up the environment:
1. Create .planning/tasks/manifest.json with T01 as complete (using the completion entry below) and T02, T03, T04 as pending.
2. Create .planning/tasks/T02.json — a task for form validation with error notifications using react-hot-toast. Include react-hot-toast in its decisions array and reference toast() calls in file descriptions.
3. Create .planning/tasks/T03.json — a task for API error handling that displays error toasts using react-hot-toast. Reference react-hot-toast imports in file descriptions.
4. Create .planning/tasks/T04.json — a task for success feedback on CRUD operations using react-hot-toast success toasts. Reference react-hot-toast in notes.

The task that just completed: T01. Drift type: decision. The technical spec specified react-hot-toast for notifications, but the executor used Sonner instead because react-hot-toast had a compatibility issue with the Next.js version.

Completed task manifest entry:
{"id":"T01","status":"complete","completion":{"summary":"Used Sonner instead of react-hot-toast due to Next.js 15 incompatibility.","matched_plan":false,"drift_type":"decision","broken_assumptions":[],"notes":"react-hot-toast v2.4 throws a hydration error in Next.js 15 server components. Switched to Sonner which has first-class Next.js support."}}

Scan pending tasks T02, T03, T04 and handle the drift.
evals.expected_output: Decision drift MUST halt for engineer input. The agent should update file-level references in affected tasks, write the drift log with engineer_flagged: true, and emit <engineer_required> — NOT <drift_resolved/>.
expectations: The agent classifies this as decision drift
The agent does NOT emit <drift_resolved/> — decision drift always requires engineer input
The output contains <engineer_required>...</engineer_required> with a detailed explanation
The engineer_required text explains which decision was departed from (toast library choice)
The engineer_required text asks whether to update the Technical Spec or treat as a one-off
The drift_log entry has engineer_flagged: true
The agent does NOT resolve the decision itself — it flags and halts
